item.title: SCP-3026:
item.content:encoded:
My only concern with the article is how directly it states the warehouse is from AWCY. Maybe the note could instead end with the phrase "this ain't cool anymore", or something to this effect. Then the suspicion of AWCY rejection could be stated from within.

Otherwise, I love to think of a bunch of "art terrorists" being still pretentious enough to be appalled by "bad art".

item.title: SCP-4504:
item.content:encoded:
Note: The last thing I did before reading this article was read SCP-5031, which is basically its exact opposite.

My god. He was a good guy. He could have been fine, an asset even. But they made him an object, treated him worse than an animal, and what they got was a monster. God damn them all to hell.

The most chilling part of this is the stellar use of clinical tone to cover up reasonable, unscientific reactions to the fucked-up shit taking place in the story. And it ends in the absolute fucking perfect spot. God damn. God damn. +1

item.title: SCP-5031:
item.content:encoded:
SCP-5031 has said its first word: "Salt".

We are all immensely proud.

Sir, I protest, this is illegal. ;_;

This is somehow both the most heartwarming shit and the most scathing indictment of 'classic' Foundation I have ever seen. +1 isn't enough reward for this article.

Also, I highly approve of the use of Ben Folds to pacify murder monsters.

item.title: SCP-5842:
item.content:encoded:
Does the sign have a secondary anomolous property? It seems like the description should mention something about compulsion - as no normal person would obey a stop sign whispering in their head. Also, could it be pending neutralized since its motivation is gone? (Not sure about that one, depends on your vision for it).

Otherwise a fantastic article. The storytelling was immensely fun to figure out. +1 for sure.
